Source: The episodes began several years ago and are accompanied by nausea and bright spots in her vision.
She has 2 glasses of wine with dinner several nights a week and has never smoked.
A 28-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider with a headache.
Her medical history is significant for acne, hypothyroidism, obesity, and endometriosis.
The patient denies any weakness, numbness, or tingling during these episodes.
A CT of the head is performed and shows no acute abnormalities.
Every few weeks she has an episode of a right-sided, throbbing headache.
On physical exam, the patient has no focal neurologic deficits.
The headache usually subsides if she lies still in a dark, quiet room for several hours.
Her home medications include levothyroxine, oral contraceptive pills, and topical trans-retinoin.
